::: {.shift .rise}
## From the IDE to the ADE

{{< include _shift-ide.html >}}

::: {.shift-words}
::: {.shift-label}
**IDE** integrated development environment
:::

An IDE is the traditional way to work on code: built for writing it by
hand, with many panels and a steep learning curve. With agents, the chat
does most of the work, yet the editor still takes the middle of the
screen and the chat gets a narrow pane at the edge.
:::

{{< include _shift-ade.html >}}

::: {.shift-words}
::: {.shift-label}
**ADE** agentic development environment
:::

Emaki turns this around. The agent chat takes the main space, and the
sidebar groups your sessions under their projects. The supporting panels
(files, outline and the two terminals) stay hidden until you need them.
:::

:::

::: {.rule}
:::

::: {.band .rise}
## Get started

Download the app and install an agent to get started. You can also install Git and the GitHub CLI for version control.

::: {.starts}

::: {.start}
### Download Emaki

For macOS, Windows and Linux.

{{< include _download-step.html >}}
:::

::: {.start}
### Install the agents

Emaki works with Claude Code and Codex.

::: {.start-links}
[Claude Code](https://docs.claude.com/en/docs/claude-code){.pill .i-claude}
[Codex](https://developers.openai.com/codex/cli){.pill .i-codex}
:::
:::

::: {.start}
### Git (optional)

Install Git and the GitHub CLI to commit, branch and push from Emaki.

::: {.start-links}
[Git](https://git-scm.com/downloads){.pill .i-git-branch .pill-git}
[GitHub](https://cli.github.com){.pill .i-github .pill-github}
:::
:::

:::

:::

::: {.rule}
:::

::: {.band .rise}
## Main system

Sessions are listed and managed under their projects. The agent chat
takes the main space, rendered in high quality.
:::

::: {.cards .cards-2 .rise}

::: {.card}
::: {.fig data-figure="projects" aria-label="Emaki's sidebar lying flat: projects in rows, the open one with its sessions under it. The project under the pointer unfolds its sessions, and the rows below make room."}
:::
### [Projects](docs/projects.qmd)
All sessions on Emaki are project-based. Toggle on a project from your sidebar to see its agent sessions. The leading logo tells you which agent it belongs to. You can quickly create, resume, archive, or delete your session(s).
:::

::: {.card}
::: {.fig data-figure="chats" aria-label="Emaki's chat lying flat: the transcript, and the composer under it. With the pointer on the composer, the draft rises as a bubble and lands at the transcript's end."}
:::
### [Chats](docs/chats.qmd)
Agent responses are nicely rendered. The artifacts, subagents, Q&A sessions, and background tasks are all taken care of with a smooth UI. The composer supports grammar check, `@` and `/` commands, and instant toggling among your available models, modes, and efforts.
:::

:::

::: {.rule}
:::

::: {.band .rise}
## Panels

Emaki provides 4 panels, hidden by default, since they are essential but used less often than the chat.
:::

::: {.cards .cards-2 .rise}

::: {.card}
::: {.fig data-figure="files" aria-label="The files panel lying flat: the tree, and the file's pane beside it. The file under the pointer opens in the pane, drawn as its kind."}
:::
### [Files](docs/files.qmd) [⌘⇧F]{.kbd}
The files panel provides a file tree with Catppuccin icons. You can live-render, preview, and edit your files. Most major file types are supported. With the git system, you can view git changes on the file tree and trigger git commands with an intuitive UI.
:::

::: {.card}
::: {.fig data-figure="outline" aria-label="The outline beside the chat, lying flat. The entry under the pointer scrolls the chat to its round."}
:::
### [Outline](docs/outline.qmd) [⌘⇧O]{.kbd}
In agent sessions, going through the history is a pain. Emaki's outline panel uses your basic AI model to summarize past conversations so you can quickly go through and locate them.
:::

::: {.card}
::: {.fig data-figure="shell" aria-label="A terminal standing up with three tabs. The tab under the pointer comes up, and its screen types itself in."}
:::
### [Shell Terminal](docs/shell.qmd) [⌘⇧S]{.kbd}
Opening a terminal and `cd`-ing to the correct location is trivial, but repeatedly doing it is a pain. Emaki's shell terminal panel does it for you. It also supports multiple tabs. The terminal UI is based on [Kaku](https://kaku.fun), a terminal made by [tw93](https://github.com/tw93).
:::

::: {.card}
::: {.fig data-figure="agent" aria-label="The chat and the agent's own terminal standing side by side. The step under the pointer stands out of both."}
:::
### [Agent Terminal](docs/agent.qmd) [⌘⇧A]{.kbd}
If you need the original CLI layout of your agent session, this is the right panel. It supports keyboard commands and mouse scrolling. Responding in this CLI is equivalent to responding in the chat interface.
:::

:::
